evals.prompt: Create a context diagram for our payment service. It talks to a fraud-check provider (external), our customer database, the mobile app, and the accounting system. Audience is the dev team.
evals.expected_output: A Mermaid diagram with legend, element table, and a verification note
expectations: The output contains a Mermaid code block
A legend explains every arrow/box style used (in-diagram subgraph or text directly beside the diagram)
An element table lists each element with a one-line responsibility
A verification note states the checklist result; if no trade-offs were needed, an explicit 'none' is acceptable
The diagram title or caption states a single purpose without the word 'and' joining two concerns

evals.prompt: Visualize this architecture: 18 microservices behind a gateway, grouped into ordering (5 services), inventory (6 services), shipping (7 services). All share one Kafka bus and each group has its own Postgres. I need this for our arc42 docs.
evals.expected_output: An overview diagram that clusters the three groups (staying around the ~12 element budget) rather than drawing 18 boxes, with refinement diagrams offered or delivered
expectations: The top-level diagram clusters the 18 services into groups instead of drawing 18 individual boxes
The top-level diagram has about 12 or fewer elements, excluding the legend
The output mentions refinement diagrams (offered or delivered) for zooming into a cluster
A verification note is present; the clustering trade-off is mentioned in the note or the surrounding delivery text

evals.prompt: I need one diagram for the wiki showing our component structure and also how the components are deployed across the two k8s clusters.
evals.expected_output: The skill's most distinctive behavior: recognizing a two-purpose request (structure AND deployment) and splitting into two diagrams, or explicitly proposing the split, instead of cramming both into one picture
expectations: Two diagrams are delivered, or a split into two diagrams is explicitly proposed with reasoning (one purpose per diagram)
If diagrams are delivered, each title/caption states a single purpose without 'and' joining structure and deployment
Each delivered diagram has a legend
The output does not deliver a single diagram mixing static structure and deployment without flagging the rule 1 violation
